papers.title: Characterization of the Intermetallic Phases in Ti/Zn and TiAlV/Zn Composite Materials
papers.abstract: Composite materials with Ti or Ti alloy reinforcement in a Zn matrix are new, promising materials with potential applications in implantology. Infiltrating zinc into the porous titanium reinforcement of a designed implant could improve its osseointegration. In this field, it is important to avoid the formation of brittle intermetallics; therefore, understanding their growth is fundamental. This work focuses on characterizing the Ti-Zn intermetallic phases at the interface of the TiAlV/Zn and Ti/Zn composites. Samples were prepared by immersing the Ti-6Al-4V or Ti bulk material in zinc melt at various temperatures. After various dwell times, the samples (pieces of Ti-6Al-4V or Ti in the molten zinc) were removed from the furnace and cooled in air. The sequence of evolution of intermetallic phases was observed to be dependent on dwell time at selected temperatures. The influences of surface treatment methods on the boundary structure were also tested.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究TiAlV/Zn复合材料中界面金属间相，不涉及增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理及其疲劳/力学性能。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not study any post-processing treatment (e.g., heat treatment, HIP, shot peening) on AM Ti-6Al-4V; instead it characterizes intermetallic phases in a Ti/Zn composite material, which is outside the scope of Layer 2 focus.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究Ti/Zn复合材料中脆性金属间相的形成，以避免影响植入物骨整合。
summary_zh.method: 将Ti-6Al-4V或Ti块浸入锌熔体中不同时间，观察界面相演变。
summary_zh.result: 发现金属间相的演变顺序依赖于保温时间和温度，表面处理也有影响。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验样品的微观结构表征验证相形成。

summary_en.motivation: To understand the formation of brittle intermetallic phases in Ti/Zn composite materials that could impair implant osseointegration.
summary_en.method: Ti-6Al-4V or Ti bulk specimens were immersed in molten zinc for varied dwell times to study interfacial phase evolution.
summary_en.result: The sequence of intermetallic phase evolution was found to depend on dwell time and temperature, with surface treatments also affecting the boundary structure.
summary_en.validation: Experimental microstructural characterization of the samples was performed to validate phase formation.

papers.title: Insights into the microstructure and coating integrity of TiO2 coatings on conventional and laser shock peened Ti–6Al–4V alloy
papers.abstract: Widely explored for its ability to improve surface and mechanical characteristics, Laser Shock Peening was evaluated in this study by comparing microstructural features, mechanical behavior, and coating robustness of Ti-6Al-4V substrates with and without peening. To improve substrate protection, TiO 2 was deposited by Electrophoretic Deposition, with voltage and time optimized as process parameters. Rutile TiO 2 was synthesized through the sol-gel method and confirmed by physico-chemical characterizations. An optimized deposition voltage of 70 V and 4-minutes process time were employed for LSP-ed substrates to evaluate their comparative effects against conventional Ti-6Al-4V. The microstructural studies revealed uniform, crack-free coatings at optimized parameters, with enhanced surface roughness. An increase in hardness from 659.5±15.1 HV to 952.1±34.7 HV was achieved through Laser Shock Peening. Similarly, the contact angle for LSP-ed coating was 19.45±0.86 °, in contrast to 30.81±0.79 ° for the unpeened, owing to the micro-surface roughness enhancement. Peened substrates demonstrated delayed crack initiation and propagation, as revealed by qualitative adhesion and scratch tests, attributed to dense dislocation networks induced by plastic deformation. Our findings establish the superiority of peened substrates over the conventional counterparts, as reflected in superior microstructural integrity and mechanical properties, positioning it as a promising surface modification approach for orthopedic bioimplants. • Rutile TiO 2 deposited over Laser shock peened and unpeened Ti-6Al-4V Alloy. • Optimized voltage of 70V and process time of 4 minutes gave dense, crack free coatings. • LSP-ed coating enhanced micro-surface roughness and hence improved mechanical behaviour. • LSP-ed substrates show superiority over unpeened substrate, positioning them as promising bioimplants.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了激光冲击喷丸对Ti-6Al-4V合金显微组织和力学性能的影响，属于后处理控制范畴，与用户方向高度相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not directly measure fatigue life or cyclic loading behavior, focusing instead on coating integrity and static mechanical properties.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究激光冲击喷丸对Ti-6Al-4V合金TiO2涂层性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 溶胶-凝胶法制备金红石型TiO2，通过电泳沉积优化参数，比较有无喷丸基体。
summary_zh.result: 喷丸后硬度从659.5 HV提升至952.1 HV，接触角降低，涂层抗裂性增强。
summary_zh.validation: 微观结构观察、硬度测试、接触角测量、粘附性划痕测试。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the effect of laser shock peening on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and coating integrity of TiO2-coated Ti-6Al-4V alloy.
summary_en.method: Rutile TiO2 coatings were deposited via electrophoretic deposition on both laser shock peened and unpeened Ti-6Al-4V substrates, with process parameters optimized.
summary_en.result: Laser shock peening significantly increased hardness (from 659.5 to 952.1 HV) and improved surface roughness, resulting in enhanced coating adhesion and delayed crack initiation.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural characterization, hardness testing, contact angle measurements, and scratch adhesion tests.
